question.en: Windows says the app is unrecognised.

answer.en: The build is unsigned. Choose More info → Run anyway. If your browser flags the download, keep the file.

question.en: The browser does not trust the certificate.

answer.en: Open Settings → Certificate and click Install into Trust Store, then fully close and reopen the browser. Reload the page afterwards.

question.en: Do I need a Microsoft account?

answer.en: No. Offline accounts work out of the box. Microsoft accounts are optional and use the device-code flow — the window shows a code you type at microsoft.com/link. The proxy refreshes the Microsoft token before every server join; if the refresh fails, the connection closes and the reason is shown in chat. Compatible third-party account services can be added separately with the API root they provide.

question.en: Why does the server list query the target every time?

answer.en: There is no status cache. Every list query goes to the target live so the MOTD, player count and version are current; a slow target makes that one query wait for its answer.

Yes. The Web UI listens on http://127.0.0.1:8765 by default and opens in the desktop window or any browser. It covers start/stop, forwarding settings, logs, accounts, certificates and updates. A password can be set only when the UI is bound to a non-loopback address; loopback access never asks for one.

question.en: Can an AI client control it?

answer.en: Yes. The same listener exposes /mcp over JSON-RPC 2.0 and Streamable HTTP, with 39 tools, resources and prompts for status, configuration (and the path-route table), logs, accounts, certificates, updates and appearance. Loopback clients need no key; remote MCP uses an MCP key and is refused when a Web UI password is set without one.
Any client that accepts a wss:// address, plus plaintext ws:// clients through the fallback port. Servers are ordinary Java servers, including Forge, NeoForge and Fabric.

The program itself only contacts the update endpoint to read api/version.json. Microsoft or third-party sign-in talks to the provider you chose; account tokens stay in accounts.json on your machine, and the relay never uploads game traffic.

question.en: How do I run it on Linux or macOS?

answer.en: Download the source package from this site and run it with Python. PyInstaller cannot cross-compile, so no Linux or macOS binary is published. Install the dependencies from requirements.txt (any Python version those packages support), then run "sh start.sh" or "python3 main.py".
Yes. All seven files under /api/ are static JSON with CORS enabled: the release manifest, FAQ, features, stats, licenses, site metadata and endpoint index. See /api/ for the field reference.

The source package includes THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt with Python, CPython, pywebview, pythonnet, the WebView2 Runtime, OpenSSL, every Python standard-library module used by the app (including random, json, ssl and asyncio), every runtime dependency and the full license texts. The desktop app's About window lists each component, its license and a project link.

question.en: The EXE won't open, it crashes on launch with an error.

answer.en: Install the Visual C++ Redistributable, or run the program from source. The EXE is built with PyInstaller and requires the VC++ runtime to be present on the system. Download it from: https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe

question.en: The console prints "ANOMALY: meaningless REX prefix used".

answer.en: Ignore it. The line comes from the graphics driver, not from this program, and it does not affect any feature. If it keeps appearing while the app is running and you use an Intel iGPU, make sure the latest Intel graphics driver is installed.
